paper_topic: Adaptive rerank budgeting for video-text retrieval via cross-layer disagreement routing

nodes.text: Video-text retrieval has become increasingly important for video search, recommendation, and multimodal understanding.

State-of-the-art systems typically employ a two-stage retrieve-then-rerank pipeline: a fast embedding model retrieves candidate videos via cosine similarity, followed by an expensive reranker that scores the top-K candidates with higher fidelity (Tzachor et al., 2026).
While effective, this approach faces a fundamental efficiency-quality tradeoff: the reranker requires K forward passes per query, making K the dominant cost factor.
A key insight is that not all queries require the same reranking budget.
nodes.display_label: Not all queries need same budget

nodes.text: Some queries are “easy”—the embedding model is confident and the top candidate is likely correct—while others are “hard” and benefit substantially from deeper reranking.

Existing adaptive methods use the embedding similarity margin (the gap between top-1 and top-2 scores) as a confidence signal, but this captures only the relative ranking of top candidates, not the underlying model uncertainty.
We propose using cross-layer ranking disagreement as a more principled confidence signal.

Recent work has shown that intermediate layers of large language models encode rich, task-relevant representations (Skean et al., 2025), and that the best visual embeddings are often found in intermediate rather than final layers (Bolya et al., 2025).

Building on this insight, we observe that when different transformer layers agree on the ranking of top candidates, the model is confident; when they disagree, the query is ambiguous and reranking is more likely to correct errors.

We introduce cross-layer ranking disagreement as a novel confidence signal for adaptive reranking, measuring the Jaccard distance between top-k candidate sets across transformer layers to quantify model uncertainty.
We propose a 3-tier routing architecture that maps disagreement scores to reranking budgets K ∈ {10, 60, 100}, enabling fine-grained allocation compared to binary routing schemes.

We demonstrate that our training-free method achieves +0.9 R@1 over margin-based routing on MSR-VTT and +1.5 R@1 on DiDeMo, while reducing reranking compute by approximately 70% compared to fixed K=100.

observations: FA0034 is a compact, linear motivation arc anchored on VidVec. It opens with a single Context sentence (N1), introduces the two-stage retrieve-then-rerank pipeline as the anchor Prior_Work (N2), then a contrastive Limitation on the K-cost tradeoff (N3). A second Context-pair (N4-N5) develops the 'not all queries need same budget' insight, leading into a second Limitation (N6) that critiques the existing margin-based confidence signal. Method emerges in two sentences: N7 names the proposal (cross-layer ranking disagreement) and N9 explains the operational principle, with N8 (Prior_Work on intermediate-layer representations) acting as evidentiary support between them. The Contribution block (C1-C3) is a clean 3-fork from N9 with no further branching. Three addresses edges back-link to limitations: N7->N6 (replaces margin signal), C1->N6 (Jaccard disagreement vs margin), C3->N3 (70% compute saving against K cost). The narrative arc is tight and didactic: state pipeline -> identify K-cost limit -> note query heterogeneity -> critique existing adaptive signal -> propose layer-disagreement signal -> evidence from layer-representation literature -> three crisp contributions. Note: N8 functioning as evidence inside the method block (rather than in the Prior_Work intro band) is a distinctive feature.
